chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man experiences hadath after he has raised his head from the final sajdah. He said: His salat is complete; the tashahhud in the salat is only sunnah. So he performs wudu (ablution), sits in his place or in a clean place, and then recites the tashahhud.

The proper way regarding this narration is that we understand it to apply to one who experiences hadath after the two testimonies, even if he has not completed the remainder of the testimony; then he completes his salat. But if the hadath had occurred before that, it would have been obligatory for him to repeat it from its beginning, as we have explained. As for his statement, 'the tashahhud in the salat is only sunnah,' its meaning is what goes beyond the two testimonies, as we have explained, and his instruction to repeat it after wudu is understood as recommendation.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: the testimony recited in the sitting of prayer
key_terms.السَّجْدَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ: the final prostration of the salat
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two core testimonies of faith within the tashahhud
key_terms.تَمَّتْ صَلَاتُهُ: his prayer is considered complete and valid
key_terms.يُحْدِثُ: enters a state of ritual invalidation during prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if hadath occurs after the final sajdah but before completing the tashahhud in salat?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling of one who experiences hadath after raising his head from the final sajdah in salat. It explains that the prayer is considered complete if the hadath occurred after the two testimonies of tashahhud, while what remains of the tashahhud is treated as sunnah and may be completed after wudu as a recommended act. If the hadath occurred before that point, the salat would need to be repeated.
